title: Successor RedeployMintPageViewV2 conflicts: would replace the correct index-4 mint view with one reading the disabled index-6 pooler
description: RestoreMintAtIndex4 sets pages('mint')=0x64FE, a mint-page view that reads the live index-4 pooler. The successor script RedeployMintPageViewV2 hardcodes 0x64FE as the OLD mint page to replace, and bumps its source dispatcher to the disabled index 6. Its guard require(currentMintPage == OLD) is satisfied by exactly the value RestoreMintAtIndex4 just wrote, so the guard passes and broadcasting RedeployMintPageViewV2 would swap the correct index-4 view for one pointed at the disabled index-6 pooler, breaking the mint page.
impact: If RedeployMintPageViewV2 is run after RestoreMintAtIndex4, the mint page is repointed to read a disabled index-6 pooler, breaking mint-page rendering / the mint view. The OLD==current guard gives false confidence because it is satisfied precisely by the state RestoreMintAtIndex4 leaves behind. RedeployMintPageViewV2 has NOT been run yet, so this is a latent conflict between two scripts rather than realized loss.
attackPath: RestoreMintAtIndex4 runs and sets pages('mint')=0x64FE reading live index 4.
Operator later runs RedeployMintPageViewV2, which expects OLD == 0x64FE.
require(currentMintPage == OLD) passes because the value matches what RestoreMintAtIndex4 wrote.
Script deploys a new mint-page view sourced from disabled dispatcher index 6 and points pages('mint') at it.
Mint page now reads the disabled index-6 pooler, breaking the mint view.
recommendation: Reconcile the two scripts so the successor does not treat the just-restored index-4 page as stale. Add an on-chain self-consistency check before any mint-page redeploy: verify the source dispatcherIndex is enabled and getData() returns sane values, rather than relying solely on a hardcoded OLD-page equality guard.
